Also inspected ORDER BY/LIMIT queries across core and remaining unordered multirow state consumers. activeInstance's opened_at-only ordering (encounterCombatants.ts:1647) is constrained to at most one active instance by the partial unique index. Effect deadlines, HP recovery, rest selection, scene logs, usage/reset loops, attunement, progression and slot selection use durable total keys or singleton/keyed/aggregate semantics; unordered label maps and campaign-rule reads have keyed or explicit JS-order consumers. campaignArc.ts:171 has closed_at-only ordering, but the tie probe with z-first/a-second/m-third sessions is stable across replay: SQLite uses the campaign/session primary-key index, returning a-second,m-third,z-first on both sides. Its documented contract specifies only closed_at ordering; no changed selection, state-integrity consequence or extra insertion-chronology requirement was established. This is a bounded sibling investigation, not a claim of universal query-order correctness.
S5. Duplicate durable-order writes fail the unique constraints. Migration runner applies the DDL/backfill/indexes and ledger row atomically (migrationRunner.ts:311); previous migrations are unchanged.
